question: Should OpenClaw’s iOS app ship model-mediated HealthKit summaries under this fixed aggregate and dual-opt-in privacy boundary?
rationale: Code review can verify the technical safeguards, but accepting HealthKit-to-provider disclosure and its ongoing App Store and privacy-policy obligations requires explicit maintainer product ownership.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded feature
options.body: Accept the fixed read-only aggregate after the setup defect, signed-device proof, and release privacy prerequisites are complete.

options.title: Narrow the initial surface
options.body: Reduce the included metrics or supported periods before shipping to limit the first sensitive-data capability.

options.title: Reject the HealthKit direction
options.body: Close this PR and the linked issue if model-mediated personal health context is outside the intended iOS product boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded feature
recommendation.body: Accept the fixed read-only aggregate after the setup defect, signed-device proof, and release privacy prerequisites are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged history connects steipete most strongly to the iOS node, gateway policy, setup, and documentation surfaces, in addition to originating this feature direction.
